title: Sovereign Desktop Theory Lab
objective: Turn industrial inference, caching, routing, and distillation mechanisms into bounded desktop hypotheses whose acceptance, attention, cost, runtime identity, and falsifiers are frozen before execution.
laws: A theory is a prospective claim with a named mechanism and falsifier, never a narrative upgrade.
Pass and fail observations count only when runtime identity is attested and telemetry is complete.
Provider, transport, and serialization errors remain non-decisive.
The same frozen task and external acceptance authority judge every arm.
Operator attention, wall time, compute, defects, and cost remain separate ledgers.
A treatment is supported only when every predeclared support predicate clears and no falsifier clears.
Open-weight residue may enter mechanistic capture; closed-teacher residue remains behavioral.
The original task cannot prove distilled transfer or amortization by replaying itself.

theories.title: Semantic prefill beats full-estate rereading
theories.claim: Source-bound selection and compaction will preserve accepted outcomes while cutting actual prefill compute and operator preparation on sparse-working-set tasks.
theories.mechanism: Most long-context jobs need a small evidence subset. The CPU and 4060 retrieval lane can produce a receipted packet, letting the 3090 avoid rereading irrelevant estate bytes.
theories.prediction: Selected context should use no more than 35% of full-estate prefill while matching pass rate, operator burden, and escaped defects.

support.note: Selected packet must not reduce accepted yield.
Median prefill compute must fall to 35% or less.

falsify.note: A pass-rate loss of ten points falsifies the operational claim.
More escaped defects falsify the fidelity claim.

confounds: Retrieval may leak hidden keys.
Full-context services may apply provider-side caching.
Token estimates may differ by tokenizer.
theories.falsifier: Loss of at least ten pass-rate points or any higher escaped-defect rate after equal source custody falsifies the operational claim.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Stable-prefix layout creates reusable processed context
theories.claim: Placing estate and campaign material before job-specific material will preserve output while reducing repeated prefill compute.
theories.mechanism: Prefix caches reuse only an exact leading token sequence. Dynamic-first prompts destroy the longest common prefix even when most content repeats.
theories.prediction: After the first run, stable-prefix ordering should serve at least half of admitted context from cache without changing pass rate.

support.note: Stable layout should at least double cache-read tokens.

falsify.note: No prefill reduction falsifies the mechanism.

confounds: Provider serialization may change token prefixes.
Chat templates may insert dynamic tokens before user content.
First-run cold cost must be reported separately.
theories.falsifier: The mechanism is falsified if exact stable ordering does not reduce subsequent prefill under a runtime that reports compatible prefix caching.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Persistent slot restore beats cold recompute above a prefix threshold
theories.claim: For sufficiently large stable prefixes, restoring a compatible llama.cpp slot will be cheaper than recomputing cold prefill.
theories.mechanism: Slot restoration trades storage I/O for model prefill. The crossover depends on prefix length, disk bandwidth, runtime build, and KV representation.
theories.prediction: Restore should beat cold prefill by at least 25% once the prefix crosses the measured break-even length, with identical acceptance.

falsify.note: Restore no faster than cold prefill falsifies the selected threshold.

confounds: OS page cache may warm files.
Slot serialization size may vary by runtime version.
Cold runs require model residency to be held constant.
theories.falsifier: At a frozen prefix length, restore time equal to or greater than cold prefill across three tasks falsifies that threshold.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Cache-sticky scheduling recovers more work per operator return
theories.claim: Grouping ready jobs by resident model and exact prefix will reduce model reloads and cold prefills without reducing accepted yield.
theories.mechanism: The commercial fleet routes toward cache locality. On a desktop, priority can be relaxed because elapsed time is abundant while operator returns are scarce.
theories.prediction: Cache-sticky scheduling should halve model-load time and reduce total prefill by at least 30% relative to strict priority order.
confounds: Task deadlines may make priority binding.
A tiny job set may not contain repeated runtimes or prefixes.
Resource telemetry must not double-count overlapping waves.
theories.falsifier: More operator attention or escaped defects under cache-sticky order falsifies the attention-first claim.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: The 4060 is valuable as a semantic-prefill worker
theories.claim: Running retrieval, reranking, compaction, and extraction on the 4060 before 3090 generation will increase accepted output per 3090 second and per operator minute.
theories.mechanism: The 4060 produces source-bound context artifacts, not transferable KV tensors. It frees the 3090 from low-value scanning and preserves the large card for generation or training.
theories.prediction: The split route should cut 3090 active time by at least 25% while matching pass rate and operator attention.
confounds: Cross-process artifact writing may dominate tiny jobs.
The 4060 model may have insufficient retrieval quality.
Concurrent GPU use can change CPU and disk contention.
theories.falsifier: The split is rejected for a task family if it lowers accepted yield or increases operator attention after artifacts and source receipts are held constant.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: A 4060 draft model can accelerate a 3090 target on compatible tasks
theories.claim: A small same-tokenizer draft model on the 4060 will reduce target forward passes and improve accepted tokens per second on predictable code and structured-output workloads.
theories.mechanism: Speculative decoding converts extra cheap draft compute into fewer expensive target passes. It only wins when draft acceptance and inter-device coordination exceed draft and verification overhead.
theories.prediction: At draft acceptance above 55%, the split should improve target throughput by at least 20% with identical final acceptance.
confounds: Draft and target must use a compatible tokenizer and generation contract.
PCIe and runtime queue serialization may erase the gain.
Sampling settings strongly affect acceptance.
theories.falsifier: No throughput gain or mean draft acceptance at or below 35% falsifies the selected draft configuration.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Pinned RAM is a useful hot tier for evicted KV state
theories.claim: Compatible KV restored from pinned host RAM will beat recomputation for reusable prefixes that no longer fit in VRAM.
theories.mechanism: RAM offload trades PCIe transfer for transformer prefill. It should win only when transfer time is below recompute time and reuse occurs before eviction.
theories.prediction: RAM restore should cut wall time by at least 20% with identical acceptance for prefixes above the measured crossover.

falsify.note: Unbounded host-memory pressure falsifies the desktop operating envelope.

confounds: Pinned memory may reduce system responsiveness.
Transfer can compete with model weights and other PCIe traffic.
NUMA placement may matter.
theories.falsifier: The RAM tier is rejected where restore is no faster than recompute or exceeds the declared host-memory envelope.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: NVMe is a selective cold tier, not a universal KV cache
theories.claim: NVMe restoration will beat recomputation only for very large prefixes with high reuse probability and predictable prefetch.
theories.mechanism: Disk bandwidth and latency are much lower than HBM and RAM. Async write and prefetch can hide some cost, but small or infrequent prefixes should be recomputed.
theories.prediction: Only the large-prefix treatment should clear; small-prefix NVMe restore is expected to be falsified.

falsify.note: Excessive disk traffic falsifies the operating envelope.

confounds: OS cache may convert NVMe tests into RAM tests.
Compression format changes I/O and CPU cost.
Cache file fragmentation can dominate.
theories.falsifier: The NVMe tier is rejected for any prefix class where restore is not faster than recompute after cold-page-cache control.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Block-level longest-prefix reuse survives small source revisions
theories.claim: Hashing ordered stable blocks and reusing the longest unchanged prefix will preserve more processed state than invalidating the whole pack after any source revision.
theories.mechanism: Transformer prefix reuse is contiguous. A later-block change should invalidate that block and its suffix, not earlier unchanged blocks.
theories.prediction: Longest-prefix reuse should reduce prefill by at least 40% on append-only or late-block revisions without changing acceptance.
confounds: Chat templates may insert revision metadata at the prefix start.
Block headers must be deterministic.
A change in an early block legitimately destroys most reuse.
theories.falsifier: No prefill reduction on late-block-only revisions falsifies the block-level reuse implementation.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Every task family has a measurable compaction loss budget
theories.claim: Moderate source compaction will preserve accepted outcomes and lower prefill, while aggressive compaction will cross a family-specific failure boundary.
theories.mechanism: Compaction removes redundant surface area but can erase exceptions, chronology, or contradiction evidence. The useful artifact is the measured boundary, not maximum compression.
theories.prediction: A 4x compacted packet should often match raw-selected context; an 8x packet is expected to fail on evidentiary tasks.
confounds: The compactor may itself use frontier cognition.
A summary can accidentally encode the hidden key.
Compression ratios must be measured in the target tokenizer.
theories.falsifier: The operational 4x claim is falsified if pass rate loses ten points or citation correctness loses five points on fresh tasks.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Claim-lineage graphs beat embedding-only retrieval on evidentiary work
theories.claim: Combining embedding retrieval with AXM or Clifford claim-lineage constraints will improve citation correctness and forbidden-inference refusal.
theories.mechanism: Embeddings recover semantic neighbors but do not encode custody, temporal order, surface boundaries, or prohibited causal hops. Graph constraints can filter attractive but inadmissible context.
theories.prediction: The graph-constrained arm should improve citation correctness by at least five points without reducing source coverage.
confounds: Graph data may be incomplete.
Human-authored edges may leak the answer.
Embedding and graph arms must share the same source corpus.
theories.falsifier: No citation gain, lower coverage, or greater operator burden after equal source custody falsifies the added graph layer.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Context budget should scale with uncertainty and evidence burden
theories.claim: Allocating context dynamically according to unresolved claims, retrieval disagreement, and required evidence will use fewer tokens than a fixed budget while preserving accepted outcomes.
theories.mechanism: Easy tasks need little context; ambiguous tasks need more. A fixed window wastes compute on easy jobs and starves hard ones. Uncertainty can become a routing signal.
theories.prediction: Adaptive packing should cut median selected tokens by at least 30% without lowering pass rate.
confounds: Uncertainty scores may be poorly calibrated.
Hard tasks can be selected after outcome leakage.
Budget changes must not alter the acceptance contract.
theories.falsifier: A five-point pass-rate or context-recall loss falsifies the adaptive policy for that task family.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Local best-of-N can replace one frontier call on grader-rich work
theories.claim: Several cheap local attempts selected by an external grader will beat a single frontier attempt on cost per accepted result for some bounded task families.
theories.mechanism: When local pass probability is nonzero and the referee is reliable, repeated independent attempts can buy reliability without purchasing frontier judgment.
theories.prediction: Best-of-3 should match frontier pass rate with lower teacher cost and no more operator attention on bounded code and counterexample tasks.

arms.label: Three local attempts plus external selection

confounds: Local attempts must be independent.
The grader must not be visible to the solver.
Local electricity and elapsed time remain separately reported.
theories.falsifier: A ten-point pass-rate loss or greater operator burden falsifies replacement for the bounded family.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Local attempt plus frontier repair beats direct frontier execution
theories.claim: A frontier model should spend judgment tokens on a concrete failed local attempt and grader report rather than redoing all work from scratch.
theories.mechanism: The local route supplies search, implementation, and failure evidence. The frontier route diagnoses the remaining residue and emits a bounded repair.
theories.prediction: Driver-repair should cut teacher tokens or cost by at least 40% while matching direct frontier acceptance.
confounds: Bad local output may anchor the frontier.
The repair packet may exceed direct prompt size.
Grader reports must not reveal hidden answer keys.
theories.falsifier: No teacher-cost reduction or lower accepted yield falsifies the composition for that family.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Failure and repair traces teach more than final answers alone
theories.claim: Training or scaffolding on failed attempt, grader diagnosis, and accepted repair will improve a local student's transfer to fresh tasks more than an equal number of final answers.
theories.mechanism: The trace exposes the decision boundary and the mechanism of correction. Final answers hide which attractive path was wrong.
theories.prediction: With equal teacher calls and student compute, trace curricula should improve fresh-task pass rate by at least ten points.
confounds: Grader signals may leak the hidden test.
Trace length can increase training tokens.
The student may memorize task identities.
theories.falsifier: No fresh-task pass-rate improvement under equal teacher-call and compute budgets falsifies the trace advantage.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Closed-teacher residue can become local source machinery
theories.claim: A recurring closed-model advantage can be captured as a scaffold, verifier, routing rule, context compiler, curriculum, or inference policy that lets the local student clear fresh work without teacher access.
theories.mechanism: Closed weights remain unavailable, but their bounded successful behavior can be treated as a black-box specification and reproduced by a local composition.
theories.prediction: The augmented local arm should match teacher acceptance on distinct replays while using zero teacher calls.
confounds: Artifact generation may leak hidden test material.
Replay tasks must be distinct.
The artifact may encode one task rather than a family rule.
theories.falsifier: Any teacher dependency during replay, or no fresh-task improvement over native local execution, falsifies capture closure.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Open-weight residue is cheaper to capture through source and weight interventions
theories.claim: When a teacher exposes weights or runtime source, small adapters or source-level inference policies will reproduce bounded residue with fewer examples and less operator effort than behavioral scaffolds alone.
theories.mechanism: Mechanistic access permits ablation, routing instrumentation, LoRA, quantization experiments, and source-level policies that closed teachers cannot expose.
theories.prediction: The best mechanistic treatment should beat the behavioral-only treatment on pass rate or capture build cost while remaining teacher-independent.

arms.label: Prompt, context, and verifier artifacts only

falsify.note: Twice the build burden without quality gain falsifies the selected mechanistic treatment.

confounds: Mechanistic experiments may overfit the donor model.
Training compute accounting must include failed candidates.
Open weights do not reveal why a closed teacher succeeded.
theories.falsifier: If source or weight interventions provide no quality or build-cost advantage over behavioral capture, the mechanistic route is not justified for that residue.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: vLLM plus LMCache has a measurable complexity threshold on one desktop
theories.claim: WSL2 vLLM plus LMCache will beat llama.cpp persistent slots only after workload concurrency, prefix diversity, or KV tier pressure crosses a measurable threshold.
theories.mechanism: vLLM and LMCache add paged serving, automatic prefix caching, CPU or disk KV tiers, and prefetch, but they also add WSL2, service, memory, and maintenance overhead.
theories.prediction: llama.cpp should win below the threshold; vLLM plus LMCache should win only on larger concurrent or multi-prefix batches.
confounds: WSL2 GPU and filesystem overhead may dominate.
Different serving kernels may change outputs.
Configuration maturity can bias early runs.
theories.falsifier: If vLLM plus LMCache does not increase accepted jobs per attention hour after its maintenance cost is charged, the added stack is rejected.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: True prefill/decode disaggregation is probably uneconomic on consumer PCIe
theories.claim: Moving model-specific KV from a 4060 prefill worker to a 3090 decode worker will not outperform aggregated 3090 serving for the models and prompts that fit this desktop.
theories.mechanism: Industrial disaggregation relies on identical model state and very fast KV transfer. Consumer PCIe, asymmetric VRAM, and duplicated model residency make transfer and setup likely more expensive than recomputation.
theories.prediction: The disaggregated arm is expected to be slower or impossible for most useful target models; a win would identify a narrow supported regime.

arms.label: Same-model prefill on 4060, KV transfer, decode on 3090

confounds: The same model may not fit on the 4060.
Runtime support may be experimental.
Transfer telemetry must distinguish TCP, host staging, and direct peer access.
theories.falsifier: The working default remains aggregated if transfer plus duplicated residency is no faster than 3090 recomputation.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Unlimited unattended local time replaces frontier calls on bounded work
theories.claim: For grader-rich tasks without hard latency requirements, a bounded local retry policy can recover most accepted work while consuming less operator attention and frontier cost.
theories.mechanism: The desktop has abundant elapsed time. Independent local attempts, external grading, and deterministic stopping can trade hours of compute for minutes of human attention.
theories.prediction: Within an overnight deadline, local retries should match frontier pass rate with lower teacher cost and no more operator interventions.

arms.label: Bounded local retries until acceptance or deadline

confounds: Retries may not be independent.
A visible grader can be gamed.
Energy and hardware wear remain reported even when dollar cost is zero.
theories.falsifier: A ten-point pass-rate loss or more interventions falsifies the unattended replacement policy.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Disagreement-selected teacher calls beat random distillation examples
theories.claim: Teacher calls chosen where local candidates disagree, fail hidden checks, or express calibrated uncertainty will produce a stronger student per teacher call than random sampling.
theories.mechanism: The teacher is most valuable at the local decision boundary. Repeatedly asking it easy questions purchases little new residue.
theories.prediction: Active selection should reach the same fresh-task pass rate with at most half the teacher calls.
confounds: Uncertainty may be miscalibrated.
Selection can overfit current validators.
Candidate pool construction may leak outcomes.
theories.falsifier: No teacher-call reduction at equal fresh-task performance falsifies the active-selection policy.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.

theories.title: Context compiler quality explains more variance than model size on recurring work
theories.claim: After a competent local model threshold, the quality of source selection, ordering, compaction, and external verification will explain more accepted-outcome variance than moving one model size rung upward.
theories.mechanism: Frontier systems often appear to possess long memory because their execution plane supplies better context and tool state. Improving the plane may move the waterline farther than increasing parameter count.
theories.prediction: A smaller model with the strong context compiler should match or beat the larger model with naive context on at least half of recurring task families.

arms.label: Smaller model with source-bound compiler and verifier

confounds: The small and large model may use different tokenizers.
Context compiler development cost must be amortized.
Some tasks may contain irreducible model residue.
theories.falsifier: If the strong context plane cannot close at least half the accepted-yield gap on fresh recurring tasks, model capability remains the dominant variable.
theories.failure_default: PARTIAL; preserve the theory and the contaminated evidence separately.
